source.title: An integrative theory of locus coeruleus-norepinephrine function: adaptive gain and optimal performance

confidence_rationale: Foundational, extremely well-replicated review establishing that phasic LC firing IS decision-locked (~90-150ms latency around a discrimination/target-detection decision, brief 3-4-spike bursts) and is proposed to modulate downstream target-neuron gain at that same short timescale -- this licenses 'decision-time LC effects' as a real phenomenon in principle. Confidence held at moderate rather than high because the entire empirical base for the theory is cortical/decision-network gain modulation (LIP, cingulate, sensory cortex target-detection), not hippocampal attractor dynamics -- it establishes plausibility, not applicability to MECH-075's specific dorsal-HPC operationalization.
failure_signatures: Phasic LC excitatory responses to target cues occur at short latency (~90-150ms) and consist of only 3-4 action potentials followed by a long refractory period -- the effect window per burst is brief, not sustained
The theory's evidentiary base is cortical target-detection and decision-network gain (LIP, ACC, OFC afferents to LC), not hippocampal attractor geometry
Tonic vs phasic LC modes map onto exploration vs exploitation over a task, not onto within-single-decision attractor width

mapping.source_claim_statement: LC neurons fire phasically, time-locked to the outcome of a task-related decision process (~90-150ms latency), and this phasic activation is proposed to transiently increase the gain of target-neuron populations engaged by that decision, facilitating the ensuing behavior. Tonic LC mode (high baseline, low phasic responsivity) instead tracks disengagement/exploration over longer task epochs.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the strongest available theoretical grounding for treating an LC-arousal signal as decision-time-relevant at all: if phasic LC bursts are decision-locked and modulate target-population gain within that same short window, then a CEM-decision-time gain manipulation (V3-EXQ-905a's basin_width read) is not obviously the wrong timescale on priors. But the theory's target populations throughout are cortical decision/attention circuits, never hippocampal attractor networks -- it licenses 'LC can act fast' in general, not 'LC widens hippocampal attractor basins within one decision' specifically.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a theoretical/review synthesis of primarily cortical and oculomotor decision-circuit data (target-detection tasks, LIP/ACC/OFC), not hippocampal electrophysiology. It answers question (b) from the /lit-pull brief (is decision-time even a plausible LC timescale at all) with a qualified yes for cortical gain, but says nothing directly about whether the SAME fast-gain mechanism extends to dorsal-HPC attractor basin geometry -- that extension is the exact gap MECH-075's dorsal leg needs and this paper does not close it.
mapping.source_context: Cross-species review (primarily macaque electrophysiology, target-detection/oddball vigilance tasks) synthesizing LC single-unit recording literature; not hippocampus-specific.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical, heavily-cited theory paper -- source quality is very high. Mapping fidelity is deliberately kept low: the paper's decision-time claims are about cortical/oculomotor gain, and applying them to hippocampal attractor-basin width is an unsupported extrapolation the paper itself never makes. Transfer risk elevated for the same reason -- moving from 'LC modulates cortical target-neuron gain within ~150ms of a decision' to 'LC widens dorsal-HPC attractor basins within a single CEM decision step' skips an entire mechanistic and anatomical step.
